text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Canary rollout roll-20260402-17 (model: v3.1.0) -> elevated 5xx and TokenizerException observed. error-rate 3.2% (alert threshold 0.5%). Auto-paging oncall + release-owner. https://console.redwood/rollouts/roll-20260402-17

noah: seeing spikes on /chat.generate from canary-pool-a. many 500s with TokenizerException: 'vocab table size mismatch (expected 50256, actual 49980)'. Also some responses truncated to empty string.

ayana: can you paste a sample request/response? only affects UTF8-heavy prompts?

noah: sample failing request:
```json
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"こんにちは — testing emoji 600 and cyrillic Привет"}]}
```
failed response body:
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"TokenizerException: vocab_len 49980 != expected 50256 at tokenizer/loader.py:87"}
```

kevin: confirmed on canary-1 and canary-4. Canary traffic ~1.8%. Latency up ~25ms, 5xx baseline 0.15% -> 3.2%. Model loader logs show weight checksum mismatch: expected sha256: 9f8e... but weights loaded as 8a7b... . Tokenizer artifact registered as tok-v4.3 but runtime picked tok-v4.2 on some nodes.

incident-bot: rollout metadata: promoted artifacts: model:v3.1.0, weights:weights-20260402-batch, tokenizer:tok-v4.3. Promotion job prom-20260402-9 had warning: 'artifact-store delay' but completed with --promote-on-warning=true.

ayana: that's the root cause smell — promotion allowed despite inter-artifact inconsistency. we should stop the canary. flipping kill-switch: `emergency-rollout-kill` -> true.

oncall-bot: @kevin you are oncall for INC-2026-401. Please acknowledge.

kevin: ack. running pause: `curl -s -X POST https://ops-api/rollouts/roll-20260402-17/actions -d '{"action":"pause"}'` -> 200 OK. Canary routing set to 0%. Traffic falling back to v3.0.9.

noah: running checksum verifier across canary pods: `kubectl exec -it pod/canary-1 -- /usr/local/bin/verify-artifacts --model model:v3.1.0`

kevin: one node shows mismatch log: `tokenizer registry: expected tok-v4.3 sha=ab12cd.. present tok-v4.2 sha=aa11bb..` so nodes have mixed tokenizer versions. Evidence of artifact mirroring lag + parallel promotion.

ayana: mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout (done). 2) Force rollback to v3.0.9 on canary pool. 3) Run full artifact checksum sweep. 4) Disable `--promote-on-warning` by default. 5) Create hotfix to promotion job to promote atomically or fail.

incident-bot: rollback job queued -> rb-2251-02-01. estimated completion 60s.

kevin: rollback finished, health checks green. 5xx back to baseline 0.12%. tokenizer exceptions dropped to 0.05%.

cs-team-bot: CS impact: 9 users exposed to 500s in last 10m; 4 paying customers (1 enterprise) reported. Drafted customer note and sent to affected account owners.

noah: capturing short timeline and immediate artifacts: prom-20260402-9 logs, node /var/log/inference/container.log, `verify-artifacts` output. Also found PR that changed artifact promotion flags last month — will link.

ayana: handoff: I'll take next steps for postmortem and pipeline hotfix. kevin handing back to ayana. summary for postmortem: non-atomic artifact promotion + permissive promote flag allowed mixed tokenizer/weights to be served in canary; canary caught regression; paused and rolled back within ~6 minutes; limited customer impact. action items: atomic promotion or checksum gate, pre-promote compatibility test (tokenizer vs weights), reduce promote permission TTL, and consider canary isolation by region until promotion verified.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Next oncall: ayana. INC-2026-401 -> status: mitigated, severity: sev2.

kevin: adding quick reproduction snippet for eng-runtime:
```bash
# reproduce check
curl -X POST https://ops-api/rollouts/roll-20260402-17/actions -d '{"action":"verify"}'
# or run local verifier
verify-artifacts --artifact-dir s3://artifacts/prod/roll-20260402-17 --expect-checksums checksums.json
```

ayana: thanks everyone. I'll open the incident doc, assign owners for each action item, and schedule a 90-minute blameless postmortem tomorrow. Pinged #eng-runtime #eng-ml #release-eng. :white_check_mark:
